This sync mode combines two rows in the destination and uses the most recent data, a vendor-managed contrast to this topic's own hand-built LSN tiebreak

The first predict question is checked specifically against what a comparison-free merge actually does (keeps whichever change was merged last) rather than against a vague claim that a periodic strategy is 'slower and therefore safer,' since the measured proof shows the naive merge fails identically whether it runs continuously or periodically.

items.item: The LSN-ordering claim is checked by actually running the same real decoded events through the same MERGE logic twice, in true order and in reversed order, rather than asserted from the documentation alone, so the convergence claim is a measured result, not a restatement of CHAPTER.md's own text.

items.item: The compaction-cost claim is checked at two concretely different update rates on the same twenty keys, with the superseded-row count read directly off the hand-built data-file table rather than estimated, so the 'proportional to update rate' claim is a measured ratio (exactly five times), not an approximation.
